items.title: What the Academie recommends instead of 'email'
items.claim: The Academie francaise has recommended a French alternative to 'email'. What is it?
items.reveal:
Quebec coined 'courriel' first; the Academie endorsed it in 2003. Similar recommendations include 'mot-diese' (hashtag) and 'jeu video en nuage' (cloud gaming).

Usage in France varies; 'mail' and 'email' remain common in practice.
items.why: Official terminology and everyday usage often diverge, sometimes lastingly.

items.title: Where most French speakers will live
items.claim: OIF (Observatoire de la langue francaise) projections suggest that by 2050, roughly what share of French speakers will live in Africa?
items.reveal_title: Most French speakers will be African
items.reveal:
OIF estimates (Demographie et langue francaise reports) project that demographic growth in francophone Africa will lift the African share of French speakers to around 85% by 2050.

This follows from population growth in countries such as DR Congo, where French is an official or working language.
items.why: The geographic centre of a language can shift dramatically across a generation.

items.title: When 'iel' entered Le Robert
items.claim: Le Robert added the gender-neutral pronoun 'iel' (combining il and elle) to its online edition in which year?
items.reveal:
The inclusion drew commentary from the Education Minister and politicians. The Academie francaise has been sceptical of inclusive writing more broadly.

Dictionaries describe usage rather than prescribe it.
items.why: Dictionary inclusions of contested terms become flashpoints in language politics.
